focus_areas: Anatomical correctness of the gular pouch and bill structure.
Texture consistency of feathers vs. background elements.
Spatial grounding of legs into the sand (depth/contact shadows).
Visibility and structure of webbed feet.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the intersection of the pelicans' feet with the sand. Use the geometric depth auditor to confirm if the legs are physically grounded or if they exhibit 'melting' artifacts. Verify that the open vocabulary detector successfully isolates each bird to prevent topological fusion errors in the boundary audit. Specifically check if the 'webbed toes' are visible enough for the pose auditor to validate, or if they remain occluded.
image_description: A group of Australian Pelicans standing on a sandy shore next to blue water. The birds feature white plumage with black flight feathers, long pinkish bills with large gular pouches, and long necks. One pelican is in the foreground left, another in the center-right, and parts of others are visible on the edges.
